result.topic_en: Euler introduces abbreviations for exponential friction factors, derives the efflux velocity of water from a vessel with friction, approximates it to first order in the friction coefficient, and recovers the frictionless result that the efflux velocity is due to the full height when the upper vessel is very wide.

352 TENTAMEN THEORIAE
$+C(1-\alpha D)h\cos.\eta+Di\cos.\theta+(1-\alpha B)(1-\alpha C)(1-\alpha D).\frac{k^4 v}{f^4}$
$+\alpha B(1-\alpha C)(1-\alpha D)\frac{k^4 v}{h^4}+\alpha C(1-\alpha D)\frac{k^4 v}{h^4}+\alpha D.\frac{k^4 v}{i^4}-v$
39. Ponatur porro ad abbreuiandum:
$e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{f}}=1-\alpha A=\mathfrak{A}$; $e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}=1-\alpha B=\mathfrak{B}$
$e^{\frac{-\alpha c}{h}}=1-\alpha C=\mathfrak{C}$; $e^{\frac{-\alpha d}{i}}=1-\alpha D=\mathfrak{D}$
tum vero:
$\frac{k^4}{f^4}=\mathfrak{f}$; $\frac{k^4}{g^4}=\mathfrak{g}$; $\frac{k^4}{h^4}=\mathfrak{h}$; et $\frac{k^4}{i^4}=\mathfrak{i}$ erit
$v=\frac{A\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}f+B\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}g\cos.\zeta+C\mathfrak{D}h\cos.\eta+Di\cos.\theta-l+\mathfrak{A}\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}\mathfrak{f}}{1-\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}\mathfrak{f}-\alpha B\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{D}\mathfrak{g}-\alpha C\mathfrak{D}\mathfrak{h}-\alpha D\mathfrak{i}}$
vbi $a+b\cos.\zeta+c\cos.\eta+d\cos.\theta$ eſt altitudo aquae ſupremae AA ſupra orificium EE.
40. Si omnes poteſtates ipſius $\alpha$ praeter primam negligamus, reperiemus:
$v=\frac{\left\{\begin{array}{ll}a+b\cos.\zeta+c\cos.\eta+d\cos.\theta-\alpha a(\frac{a}{2f}+\frac{b}{g}+\frac{c}{h}+\frac{d}{i}) & \\ -\alpha l(\frac{a}{f}+\frac{b}{g}+\frac{c}{h}+\frac{d}{i}) & -\alpha b\cos.\zeta(\frac{b}{2g}+\frac{c}{h}+\frac{d}{c}) \\ & -\alpha c\cos.\eta(\frac{c}{2h}+\frac{d}{i}) \\ & -\alpha d\cos.\theta.(\frac{d}{2i}\end{array}\right\}}{1-\mathfrak{f}+\alpha\mathfrak{f}(\frac{b}{g}+\frac{c}{h}+\frac{d}{i})-\alpha\mathfrak{g}.\frac{b}{g}-\alpha\mathfrak{h}.\frac{c}{h}-\alpha\mathfrak{i}.\frac{d}{i}}$
et ſi nulla plane eſſet frictio, ſeu $\alpha=0$, foret:
$v=\frac{a+b\cos.\zeta+c\cos.\eta+d\cos.\theta}{1-\mathfrak{f}}$
vnde poſita tota altitudine $AI=q$, erit $v=\frac{f^4}{f^4-k^4}.q$
41. In tranſitu hic obſeruo, ſi amplitudo vaſis ſupremi ſit maxima prae amplitudine orificii, fore $v=q$, ſeu celeritatem effluxus in EE debitam eſſe altitudini AI$=q$, vti per conſueta principia conſtat. Sin autem

items.english: If the width of the uppermost vessel is very large compared with the width of the orifice, then v = q, i.e. the efflux velocity at EE is that due to the height AI = q, as is established by the usual principles.
